column2: Ask 10 simulated online-banking customers one open question: what would most improve our mobile banking app? Summarize the themes with counts.

Build a survey for software users: first a yes/no question whether they used the export feature; if No, the survey ends. Then ask what problem they hit, and then what would resolve that problem, piping their problem into the last question. Show me the survey flow and the exact prompts before running.

Test two instruction messages, 'Export your report.' and 'Download your report as a CSV file.', with four profiles: new or experienced users who are individual contributors or team leads. Ask how clear each message is (Clear, Unclear, Unsure) and a 0 to 10 clarity score. Chart the clarity distribution and the mean score by message.

Here is customer feedback as CSV:

f1,The setup was easy.
f2,The export button is missing.
f3,Support took three days to reply.

And profiles:
profile_id,experience
p1,new user
p2,frequent user

Load both, have each profile classify each feedback as Positive, Neutral or Negative, and show record_id, profile and sentiment.

Code these customer requests with a codebook: Billing (a charge or payment issue), Access (cannot enter a page), Feature request. Requests: 'I was charged twice', 'I cannot reset my password', 'Please add a dark theme', 'My invoice shows the wrong amount'. Use a checkbox of the codes plus a free-text question quoting the evidence, then tally the codes.

Pretest two survey items before I field them: 'Do you use this service regularly?' and 'On how many of the past 7 days did you use this service?'. Have two reviewer agents, one that reads literally and one that infers intent, pick the main issue (Ambiguous timeframe, Double-barreled, Leading, None identified) and propose a revised wording. Show me the exact prompts.

Run a one-question survey, how clear is a message (Clear, Unclear, Unsure), with two messages ('Export your report.' and 'Download your report as a CSV file.') and two respondent roles (individual contributor, team lead). Then run it again exactly the same and tell me how many answers came from the cache. Then export condition, role and clarity as a CSV filtered to the short message.

Draft five diverse customer personas for a landscaping company with different satisfaction levels. Run an NPS survey: a 0 to 10 recommend question, then separate 1 to 5 ratings for product quality, customer support and purchasing. Chart the NPS and the mean ratings.

Run a two-pass theme study on these course evaluations: 'Great pace, clear slides', 'Too fast but good examples', 'Slides were hard to read', 'Loved the hands-on labs'. Pass 1 asks for up to three themes per evaluation. Pass 2 builds a codebook from the distinct themes and codes every evaluation with a checkbox of those themes plus 'None of these'. Show the theme counts as a chart.

Interview a panel of six college students about the career they want. Then add each answer as a trait on that agent and run a follow-up survey asking why they chose that career. Show the career and reason per student.

Design a choice-based conjoint for a phone plan with Price ($10, $20, $30), Data (5 GB, 20 GB) and Contract (None, 12 months): four tasks per respondent, three options per task. Run it for two segments, students and families. Show the attribute importance chart, the part-worth chart and the price curve, and the choice shares for $10 with 20 GB and no contract versus $30 with 5 GB and a 12-month contract.

Which video streaming services do US households under 35 versus over 55 prefer, and why? I want to know where each service is strongest.

Run an AI-moderated interview study: draft a short interview guide on how knowledge workers decide whether to go into the office, then have an EDSL interviewer conduct it with four simulated knowledge workers (two hybrid, two fully remote), with one follow-up question per answer. Summarize the themes by group.

I want real people to answer this, not simulated respondents: one multiple-choice question 'How do you usually buy coffee on workdays?' (Make at home, Cafe, Canned or bottled, I don't drink coffee). Create the human survey with Expected Parrot's humanize and give me the link to send.
Ask 'How many hours per week do you exercise?' as a numerical question to 30 simulated US adults on two models, Llama 4 Maverick and Kimi K2.5, and compare the two answer distributions with a chart.

Here is a Google Form I use, copied as text. Title: Coffee habits. Q1 (multiple choice, required) How many cups of coffee do you drink per day? 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 or more. Q2 (checkboxes) Where do you buy coffee? Cafe / Grocery store / Online / Office. Q3 (linear scale 1 to 5) How important is price? Q4 (paragraph) What would make you switch brands? Rebuild it as an EDSL survey, run it on 20 simulated office workers, and chart the results.

Validate simulated coders against my gold labels. Requests and gold codes: 'I was charged twice' = Billing; 'I cannot log in' = Access; 'Add a dark theme' = Feature request; 'Refund my last invoice' = Billing; 'The page will not load' = Access; 'Please support CSV export' = Feature request. Have 5 simulated coders label each request with the codebook, then report accuracy against gold and agreement between coders, with a confusion matrix chart.

I attached an ad image. Show it to 20 simulated shoppers (10 under 30, 10 over 50) and ask how appealing it is (1 to 5), what message they take away, and whether they would try the product. Chart the appeal ratings by group.

I attached a two-page product brief as a PDF. Load each page as a scenario and have 10 simulated brand managers answer, for each page, what the key decision is and what risk they see. Then summarize across pages with a chart of the risks named.
